title: Polishing and commercial quality workflow.
author: AcidShAwk
selftext:
I'm a long time developer. 30 years and I've only gotten faster with Claude. I've always wanted to make a game and had a concept in my head for years.

Well I finally built it with Claude. I purposely used free models, music, sound effects. To get the game itself working, mechanically, the way I want it to, before I do any polishing and visual quality enhancement. 

It how I've always built my software. Barebones ui, ensure functionality is perfect, return and polish ui. 

Well I'm at a state where the game is essentially working perfectly an MVP.  1st level, menus, start intro, credits. Etc. I used unity, focused on building it for my Mac first before I target other platforms..

What I'm wondering is, can I run an automated pass through Claude with a specific workflow where it can handle this polishing pass on its own. That includes taking the free models, and enhancing them? 

The game isn't in a rough state. But it's clearly an amateur quality game and I want to get it to a professional quality state.

For the final game, I have 24 levels, 5 bosses. And a future of additional content downloads with tougher challenges..

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
Claude is good at getting low quality prototypes out and you do the polishing later.

You are going at it the opposite way and it's not going to work out well imo.

comments.author: random_boss
comments.body: You’ll probably be able to get some amount of polish out of it, but I don’t think you’re going to be able to do what you’re trying to do. The lack of polish you’re noticing is due to taste. You have it, Claude necessarily doesn’t (if it did we wouldn’t be inundated with slop on all sides). This is part where you need to be giving millions of little specific changes

comments.author: PaperTigerDev
comments.body: You need to know what you want. Your job is to break down the vision of your game into managable chunks. AI can do the rest but it cannot do the vision for you and it doesn't know what feels like fun and what doesn't.

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body: After all the work you put in, do you even want Claude doing the polishing? That's where you're voice, style, aesthetic and tone come out and if you leave it to Claude it'll generate you a middle of the road solution. That's fine, if that's what you want.

replies.author: AcidShAwk
replies.body: There are tools that can generate the style I'm going for. Things I have working really well are the movement mechanics. Parkour style player movement for example. Jumping walls, running, seem to work really well. The issue is the character design, the models, seem fairly lacklustre. I'm not an artist and realise I can pay for others to make models, but I'd rather come up with an automated solution if it's achievable.
